title: Nonnegativity of the mixed payoff against a pure column
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M$ row actions and $N$ column actions, let $p$ be a mixed row strategy over the $M$ rows, and let $j$ be a pure column action. Then the expected payoff of $p$ against column $j$ is non-negative:
\[
  \sum_{i} p_i \cdot A_{ij} \;\ge\; 0.
\]
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite zero-sum game with M rows and N columns (payoff entries in [0,1])
p is a mixed row strategy over the M rows (nonnegative weights summing to 1)
j is a pure column action
replaced:
For any game $G$, mixed row strategy $p$, and pure column action $j$,
$\mathrm{payoffVsPure}(G,p,j) \geq 0$.
